profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC10 sits at 22210 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus; this record shares its address with CloudHQ LC9, also tracked separately in this dataset, since both derive from a single project address recorded by a third-party aggregator rather than individually distinct street addresses published by CloudHQ itself. CloudHQ's own current campus page places the site directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing it as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available, a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building; no third-party aggregator figure specific to LC10 alone was found either. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide and over 6,000 megawatts of further expansion potential, figures CloudHQ discloses on its own homepage alongside a stated 5.2-gigawatt global data center inventory.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC10 is one of fourteen buildings on the LC Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, sharing a single address with LC9 according to third-party records. The full LC Campus totals approximately 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across all fourteen buildings, with 756 megawatts available for new tenants, but CloudHQ does not publish capacity figures broken out by individual building. No building-level specifications for LC10 alone were found from CloudHQ or other sources.

The LC Campus sits directly off Loudoun County Parkway in the heart of Ashburn, the world's densest concentration of data center capacity, where dozens of competing operators have built within a few miles of one another. Virginia's published data center capacity totals 1,375 megawatts across twenty-three facilities with disclosed specifications; the full LC Campus ranks twenty-fourth among all published capacity figures in the state, though that ranking reflects the fourteen-building campus as a single entity rather than LC10's share alone. The power utility for the campus is not published by CloudHQ; Dominion Energy is the dominant utility across Loudoun County.

The LC Campus qualifications and certifications are not published by CloudHQ in the materials available. CloudHQ does not name specific tenants at LC10 or the broader campus, and no third-party source identified which hyperscalers or other operators occupy space there.
